newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's Q3 income outside U.S. rises.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's Q3 income outside U.S. rises.

text.p: McDonald's Corp said Friday its operating income outside the United States rose 11 percent in the third quarter, compared with a 25 percent gain a year ago.

Systemwide sales for the third quarter rose nine percent, compared with a 24 percent rise last year. Company revenues outside the United States rose 13 percent compared with a 25 percent increase last year, it added.
For the first nine months, operating income outside the United States rose nine percent, while systemwide sales gained 10 percent and company revenues were up 14 percent.
McDonald's said expansion outside the United States was responsible for sales increases, offset in part by weaker foreign currencies.

The difference between the percentage increases in sales and revenue for the third quarter and nine months was primarily due to the weakening Japanese yen, which had a greater effect on sales versus revenues, as well as a higher growth rate in company-operated versus franchised restaurants.
If exchange rates had remained at 1995 levels, sales outside the United States would have increased 15 percent and 14 percent for the nine months and the third quarter, respectively.
Of the 15 largest international markets, strong sales and operating income growth for the nine-month period were seen in Japan, Hong Kong, England, Italy, Spain and Sweden.
For the third quarter, Hong Kong, England, Italy, Spain, Sweden and Taiwan had strong sales and operating income growth.
In Latin America, Brazil's results were good compared with an exceptional performance last year, the company said.

Results in Mexico continued to be weak due to economic and currency factors. McDonald's added it expects Mexico will offer long-term potential and is encouraged by recently improved operating results.
McDonald's said its business in Canada, France and Germany continued to be hurt by weak economies.

Excluding weaker foreign currencies and a $16 million non-cash charge for asset impairment in Mexico, operating income outside the United States increased 13 percent for the nine-month period and 14 percent for the third quarter.
